competences: The learner identifies sourced facts about child labour.
The learner explains information relating to Children's rights and child labour.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads and spells: child labour, children, rights, work.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state facts about child labour.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer original sourced questions on Children's rights and child labour.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied related ideas about Uganda and its population or government. They use this knowledge in studying child labour.
materials: P5 SST notes about Children's rights and child labour
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to recall earlier Social Studies work and introduces child labour. They ask the original question "Give any two ways children are subjected to child labour in the society today." and note the learners' responses before teaching the content.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work, answer the opening question and explain what they already know about Uganda and its people.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about child labour

By sensitising children about their rights. By educating the public on children’s rights It leads to death of children - early marriage It leads to street children
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Meaning and key facts about child labour", starting with "They promote the welfare of children in the society Note: The Vice chairperson is the local council I committee member who is in charge of protection of children’s rights.; Ch". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.content: Give any two ways children are subjected to child labour in the society today. | Mention two ways child labour affects children in your community. | Give any two ways children can contribute towards violation of their rights. | Give one way school children express the spirit of nationalism when on assemblies. | Why are children not allowed to vote in an election?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the exact sourced questions, beginning with "Give any two ways children are subjected to child labour in the society today." and "Mention two ways child labour affects children in your community.". They supervise the written responses, check the answers against the lesson notes and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions in their books, compare their work with the factual notes and correct wrong or incomplete answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the important facts about child labour and evaluates learning using "Give any two ways children are subjected to child labour in the society today." and "Mention two ways child labour affects children in your community.". They give guidance on the remaining original exercise for home revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, mention one important fact and make corrections in their notebooks before the lesson ends.

assessment: Use the original questions "Give any two ways children are subjected to child labour in the society today." and "Mention two ways child labour affects children in your community." and other exercises to test understanding. Mark answers and assist pupils to correct them using the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining original sourced exercise questions, especially "How is the LC I Vice-chairperson useful to children in your community?"
